exact_statement: Fix C>=0 and a nonconstant finite uniform Boolean seed f with H(f)-CI(f)>0. Pad with r dummy coordinates and flip physical vertex zero to get F_N, N=n+r. For every dummy j, average child slack sigma_j(F_N)=-(delta(f)+delta(F_(N-1)))/2 tends to -delta(f)<0. Every original coordinate slack converges to its seed slack. If all original average child slacks are strictly positive, then eventually the average-child-eligible coordinates are exactly the original coordinates and their minimum B_i/Inf_i tends to E(f), although the unrestricted minimum tends to min(E(f),2). For the three-bit point defect, N=12,C=8/3, F_N has full Fourier support, max influence<1/4 and positive delta; all original coordinates have nonnegative individual child slacks and B_i/Inf_i>5/2, while all nine dummy coordinates have both individual child slacks negative and B_j/Inf_j<5/2. Thus root selection B_i<=5Inf_i/2 does not imply selection with certified average children at C=8/3 on this class. Moreover, with Q_C(f)=min_i [B_i(f)+max(-sigma_i(f),0)]/Inf_i(f), Q_C(F_N) tends to Q_C(f) for every fixed violating seed, with no seed-child positivity assumption; every dummy corrected price is asymptotic to delta(f)*2^(N-1) and diverges.
hypotheses: Finite uniform Boolean signs; entropy in bits; normalized Walsh coefficients
The fixed seed has only relevant inputs and I(f)>0; C fixed before r tends to infinity
Eligibility means sigma_i>=0; the limiting data-only minimum assertion requires strict positivity of every original seed average child slack
The finite example is the actual three-bit one-point defect padded by nine coordinates and flipped at physical zero; no minimal-violator hypothesis is asserted

proof_dependencies.scope: Independent reconstruction of B-minimum limit and H/I continuity; original all-lambda/D statement not adopted as independently accepted here.

refutes: For every full-Fourier-support Boolean function with max_i Inf_i<1/4 and H>(8/3)I, a coordinate with B_i/Inf_i<=5/2 and average child slack>=0 exists.
